## Install

### macOS

Download the `.dmg` for your Mac — `darwin-arm64` for Apple Silicon,
`darwin-amd64` for Intel — open it and drag **K8s Dockside** to
Applications.

The app is ad-hoc signed rather than notarised, so on first launch
macOS will say it cannot be checked. Either right-click the app and
choose **Open**, or clear the quarantine flag:

```sh
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/k8sdockside.app"
```

### Windows

Run `k8sdockside-0.1.37-windows-amd64-installer.exe`.
The installer is unsigned, so SmartScreen will warn once —
**More info → Run anyway**. The `.zip` holds the bare `.exe` if you
would rather not install anything.

### Linux

Needs GTK 4 and WebKitGTK 6 at runtime; the `.deb`, `.rpm` and Arch
packages declare them, the AppImage expects them present.

```sh
# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt install ./k8sdockside-0.1.37-linux-amd64.deb

# Fedora / RHEL
sudo dnf install ./k8sdockside-0.1.37-linux-amd64.rpm

# Arch
sudo pacman -U ./k8sdockside-0.1.37-linux-amd64.pkg.tar.zst

# Anywhere else
chmod +x k8sdockside-0.1.37-linux-amd64.AppImage
./k8sdockside-0.1.37-linux-amd64.AppImage
```

Every asset is listed in `checksums.txt`:

```sh
  checksums.txt
```

Each asset also carries SLSA build provenance:

```sh
gh attestation verify <file> --repo k8sdockside/k8sdockside
```

An SPDX SBOM of the build is attached as

## Install

### macOS

Download the `.dmg` for your Mac — `darwin-arm64` for Apple Silicon,
`darwin-amd64` for Intel — open it and drag **K8s Dockside** to
Applications.

The app is ad-hoc signed rather than notarised, so on first launch
macOS will say it cannot be checked. Either right-click the app and
choose **Open**, or clear the quarantine flag:

```sh
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/k8sdockside.app"
```

### Windows

Run `k8sdockside-0.1.8-windows-amd64-installer.exe`.
The installer is unsigned, so SmartScreen will warn once —
**More info → Run anyway**. The `.zip` holds the bare `.exe` if you
would rather not install anything.

### Linux

Needs GTK 4 and WebKitGTK 6 at runtime; the `.deb`, `.rpm` and Arch
packages declare them, the AppImage expects them present.

```sh
# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt install ./k8sdockside-0.1.8-linux-amd64.deb

# Fedora / RHEL
sudo dnf install ./k8sdockside-0.1.8-linux-amd64.rpm

# Arch
sudo pacman -U ./k8sdockside-0.1.8-linux-amd64.pkg.tar.zst

# Anywhere else
chmod +x k8sdockside-0.1.8-linux-amd64.AppImage
./k8sdockside-0.1.8-linux-amd64.AppImage
```

### Verifying a download

Every asset is listed in `checksums.txt`:

```sh
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing checksums.txt
```

`checksums.txt` is itself signed with
[cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/), keylessly — there is no
private key, only a certificate tying the signature to this
workflow and this tag:

```sh
cosign verify-blob \
  --certificate checksums.txt.pem \
  --signature checksums.txt.sig \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  --certificate-identity "https://github.com/k8sdockside/k8sdockside/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v0.1.8" \
  checksums.txt
```

Each asset also carries SLSA build provenance:

```sh
gh attestation verify <file> --repo k8sdockside/k8sdockside
```

An SPDX SBOM of the build is attached as
`k8sdockside-0.1.8-sbom.spdx.json`.

> These prove *where the file came from*. They are not code
